look_here_first: Look at the basal leaves first: huge, stiff, deeply pinnatifid blades cut almost to the midrib into narrow lobes. Then check the towering flowering stem and yellow ray-and-disk heads. Leaf north-south orientation is variable and not diagnostic by itself.

key_traits.label: Best field traits
key_traits.text: Massive deeply pinnatifid basal leaves with narrow lobes.; Very tall erect flowering stalk, often above a basal leaf rosette.; Yellow ray florets and central disk florets in sunflower-like heads.; Stiff coarse foliage; inspect leaf dissection rather than flower color.; Leaves sometimes held approximately north-south, but orientation alone is unreliable.

lookalikes.differences: S. radula has broader rough leaves rather than the extremely deeply dissected compass leaves. S. albiflorum has white rays and different leaf architecture. S. integrifolium has broad mostly entire leaves; historic Central Texas variety names need concept-level reconciliation.
